name: pageviews.js
what_it_holds: Lightweight JavaScript/Node client (Apache-2.0, Thomas Steiner, 2017, 63 commits) for the Wikimedia Pageviews API: per-article views, project totals, top articles, unique-device counts by time granularity.
why_useful: Another mature client if any tooling needs to run in a JS/Node context (e.g. a dashboard); same underlying data source as the Python/R clients above.
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: Another mature client if any tooling needs to run in a JS/Node context (e.g. a dashboard); same underlying data source as the Python/R clients above.

A JS alternative to python-mwviews/waxer for the same pageviews-as-engagement-proxy use case; only worth using if the team ever needs a browser/Node-side pull (e.g. a lightweight dashboard) rather than a Python/R backtest pipeline.

name: pvduck
what_it_holds: Tool to aggregate raw Wikimedia pageviews DUMP files (the https://dumps.wikimedia.org/other/pageviews/ hourly dumps, not the aggregated REST API) directly into a DuckDB database, letting you query pageviews at scale without downloading/parsing gzipped dump files by hand.
why_useful: Useful complementary tool to gap #5: the raw dumps go back further and are finer-grained (hourly, all-article) than the REST API's per-article convenience endpoint, so pvduck is the practical way to mine that firehose for a specific set of destination-city articles across years without standing up Hadoop/Spark.
time_coverage: Wikimedia pageview dumps span 2015-present (hourly raw counts)
size_hint: small tool; user supplies which dump files to ingest
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: Useful complementary tool to gap #5: the raw dumps go back further and are finer-grained (hourly, all-article) than the REST API's per-article convenience endpoint, so pvduck is the practical way to mine that firehose for a specific set of destination-city articles across years without standing up Hadoop/Spark.

name: wikipedia-decline-llm
what_it_holds: Uses the Wikimedia Pageviews API to estimate Wikipedia traffic decline attributable to AI chatbots (LLM referral cannibalization).
why_useful: Off-theme for tourism demand but directly relevant to gap #19 (AI-referral traffic / bot-share datasets) — same pageviews API, different application: could be adapted to check whether AI-chatbot-driven decline in Wikipedia/travel-site traffic is a confound for any web-engagement-based tourism proxy the team builds.
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: Off-theme for tourism demand but directly relevant to gap #19 (AI-referral traffic / bot-share datasets) — same pageviews API, different application: could be adapted to check whether AI-chatbot-driven decline in Wikipedia/travel-site traffic is a confound for any web-engagement-based tourism proxy the team builds.

name: ai.robots.txt
what_it_holds: Curated, machine-generated list (robots.json source, MIT, 746 commits) of known AI-crawler user agents (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, etc.) exported as robots.txt/.htaccess/nginx/Caddy/HAProxy/lighttpd block-lists plus a table-of-bot-metrics.md; links out to a 'Bot Ledger' directory and an 'AI Crawler Census' that tracks allow/block status across top sites. No traffic-volume numbers in this repo itself.
why_useful: Reference list of AI-bot identifiers needed to build any AI-referral-traffic measurement (gap 19); the linked 'AI Crawler Census' (tracks which top sites block which AI bots) is a candidate to check separately for site-level allow/block time series, though not fetchable this pass (404 on darkvisitors/agents).
time_coverage: current snapshot only (list of active bots, not a volume time series)
themes: Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
why_all: Reference list of AI-bot identifiers needed to build any AI-referral-traffic measurement (gap 19); the linked 'AI Crawler Census' (tracks which top sites block which AI bots) is a candidate to check separately for site-level allow/block time series, though not fetchable this pass (404 on darkvisitors/agents).

name: AgentECHO
what_it_holds: Self-hosted analytics platform (Go/TypeScript/Next.js/ClickHouse) to detect, classify, and monetize AI bot traffic (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, etc.) on a site the operator controls; ships code only, no third-party dataset — it produces data only from traffic it observes on a deployed site.
why_useful: Illustrates current tooling for AI-crawler traffic measurement (gap 19) but has no usable pre-existing dataset for ABNB or travel; would only be useful if deployed on a site we control.
themes: Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
why_all: Illustrates current tooling for AI-crawler traffic measurement (gap 19) but has no usable pre-existing dataset for ABNB or travel; would only be useful if deployed on a site we control.
